# glinet_wan_port (Resource)

Manages the role and the MAC address of a wired WAN port of the router (`cable.set_port_config` in the router API).

~>**Warning:** `mode = "lan"` removes the wired uplink of the port, and a change of the MAC address can make the upstream network give the router a new address. Then Terraform can lose the access to the router.

Use one instance of this resource for each wired WAN port. The port always exists on the router, so create takes over the port. Only a router with a second wired WAN port (`software_feature.secondwan` of `system.get_info`) accepts `name = "secondwan"`: for that port, the provider reads `system.get_info` before each call and stops with an error when the router has no second wired WAN port. The protocol settings of the same port (DHCP, static address, PPPoE) are in `glinet_wan`, which uses another router method; the two resources have no attribute in common. Each write sends `mode` and, for `mode = "wan"`, the MAC settings, as the web UI does. Each MAC attribute that is not set keeps the value of the router: the provider sends back the value that it reads from the router just before the write. Before a change of the port from `wan` to `lan`, the provider reads `network.check_wan_cable` and stops with an error while the router reports `cable_enabled`, as the web UI does: remove the cable from the port first. The web UI waits 3 seconds after the write, or 15 seconds after a change of `mode`, before it reads the ports again; the provider does not wait. The read of the ports was seen on a router, but the values of `mac_update` and `mac_period_hours` were not. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Clone the MAC address of the device that the upstream network knows.
resource "glinet_wan_port" "this" {
  name        = "wan"
  mode        = "wan"
  mac_mode    = "clone"
  mac_address = "02:00:5E:10:00:01"
}

# A random MAC address that the router changes each week.
# Only on a router with a second wired WAN port.
resource "glinet_wan_port" "second" {
  name             = "secondwan"
  mode             = "wan"
  mac_mode         = "random"
  mac_update       = "time"
  mac_period_hours = 168
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) How the router uses the port: `wan` for an uplink or `lan` for a LAN port (`mode` in the router API). `lan` removes the wired uplink of the port.
- `name` (String) The wired WAN port: `wan` for the first port or `secondwan` for the second port (`name` in the router API). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `mac_address` (String) MAC address of the port, in lower case or upper case (`macaddr.macaddr` in the router API). Must not be `00:00:00:00:00:00` or a multicast address (the second hex digit must be even). Can be set only when `mac_mode` is `clone` or `random`, and is required for `clone`. For `random`, when it is not set, the provider sends back the MAC address of the router when the router already uses a random MAC address, and else makes a random locally administered MAC address, as the web UI does. With `mac_update` `time` or `reboot`, the router changes the MAC address itself: do not set this attribute then, or each change shows as a difference. With `mac_mode` `default`, the provider sends `default_mac_address`, as the web UI does.
- `mac_mode` (String) MAC address of the port (`macaddr.mode` in the router API): `default` for the MAC address of the router (`default_mac_address`), `clone` for the MAC address in `mac_address`, for example the MAC address of a client, or `random` for a random MAC address. Can be set only when `mode` is `wan`. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `mac_period_hours` (Number) Period in hours after which the router changes a random MAC address, for `mac_update = "time"` (`macaddr.period` in the router API). The web UI offers 1 to 180 days and sends the period in hours, so the value must be a multiple of 24 from 24 to 4320; the attribute uses the unit of the router so that the provider can send back each router value unchanged. Can be set only when `mac_mode` is `random`, and not with `mac_update = "none"`. The web UI also sends the period with `mac_update = "reboot"`; what the router does with it then is not known. When it is not set, the router value does not change, or the provider sends 168 (7 days) when the router has no value, as the web UI does.
- `mac_update` (String) When the router changes a random MAC address (`macaddr.update` in the router API): `none` never, `time` each `mac_period_hours`, `reboot` at each reboot. Can be set only when `mac_mode` is `random`. When it is not set, the router value does not change, or the provider sends `none` when the router has no value, as the web UI does.

### Read-Only

- `default_mac_address` (String) MAC address of the router for the port (`macaddr.defmacaddr` in the router API).
- `id` (String) Same as `name`.
- `label` (String) Label of the port on the case of the router (`silk` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the port: "wan" or "secondwan".
terraform import glinet_wan_port.this wan
```
